The T2 vibe came from our heroes co-opting a Super Battle Droid... and growing attached to it.|archivedate=20160305024340}} and at some point, Rex was injured.{{Twitter|BFree63|status/466826004938235905|[[Brent Friedman]]|quote=Halabrew Ha! Injuries yes, but nothing so cruel was planned.|archivedate=20190904234203}} ===The Nik Sant connection=== [[File:NikSant-ROTJ.png|thumb|right|180px|Nik Sant in ''Return of The Jedi'']] Dave Filoni speculated that Rex might be [[Nik Sant]], one of the members of the [[Special Forces Trackers Unit|Endor strike team]] from the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. "I really do think that Rex is that guy on Endor," he said, "I really do. Why else is there a bearded old guy on [[Endor]], Tano? Why? It makes no sense. If you don't want that to happen, do you know what that means? I'm gonna make that happen, I'm getting like Palpatine, I'm getting power crazy."{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/captain-rex-in-return-of-the-jedi|text=A 'Star Wars' Animated Character Might've Appeared in a Live-Action Star Wars Movie?|author=Sciretta, Peter|date=2016-03-30|work=/Film|archivedate=20200308032907}} The ''Rebels'' series finale, which aired on [[March 5]], [[2018]], confirmed that Rex did fight in the Battle of Endor, though it did not confirm whether he and Sant were the same character. Six months after the episode's airing, Filoni revealed in an interview with [[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]] he ultimately chose to not canonize the theory because he felt that laying down an already established character prior to his coming to ''Star Wars'' wasn't correct, adding that Rex could have been present at Endor and not be Sant, even though some fans could choose to believe that Rex and Sant are the same individual while other choose to not do so.{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2018/08/12/star-wars-rebels-season-4-finale-clone-wars-final-season-revival-disney-dave-filoni|text=Star Wars Rebels Creator Dave Filoni Reveals How Season 4 Almost Ended and His Clone Wars Revival Plans|author=Huver, Scott|date=2018-08-12|archivedate=20191227143521}} In [[2019]], Rex was depicted in recreations of shots from ''Return of the Jedi'', as well as original shots, in the ''[[Star Wars Galaxy of Adventures]]'' short "[[Han Solo - From Smuggler to General]]."{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars Galaxy of Adventures|text=Han Solo - From Smuggler to General|video=N_KBQ-gRgxU}} As ''Galaxy of Adventures'' is not meant to be a literal depiction of canon,{{Twitter|missingwords|status/1139593657986588675|[[Matt Martin]]|quote=I think it's just the usual GoA stuff, not meant to be taken literally.|archivefile=File:MattMartinGoA.jpg}} no source has currently stated that they are the same character. ===Contradictions=== {{Quote|I think that's where you can get hung up on continuity so much that you don't actually tell a story that's about real people. So Rex at that moment tells Kanan the point of view Kanan needs to understand who Rex is and what he's really about. Later on, do they have a scene where they get into the truth of it that was a lot scarier? Probably, but I think Kanan also knows that. So I think it takes them ''[Ahsoka and Rex]'' a long time to cope with everything. The life they knew is gone. It's tough. It would be hard because with The Clone Wars, I know where it ends.|Dave Filoni, on the supposed contradiction between Rex's statement in ''Rebels'' and Order 66 in ''The Clone Wars''|{{WebCite|url=https://nerdist.com/article/star-wars-clone-wars-final-season-dave-filoni-interview|text=Dave Filoni on the End of STAR WARS: THE CLONE WARS|author=Amy Ratcliffe|date=2020-06-10|archivedate=20200621031514}}}} [[File:OldCaptRex-GoH.png|thumb|left|275px|Rex in ''Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes'']] Before the release of ''The Clone Wars'' season seven, many sources wrongly assumed Rex removed his control chip before the execution of Order 66''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''{{FactFile2014|118|REX 5-8|Captain Rex}}{{HelmetCollectionCite|16|Helmets}}{{HelmetCollectionCite|70|Helmets}} after Rex seemingly said as such in ''Rebels''. Filoni later clarified that Rex only told Kanan Jarrus "the point of view Kanan needs to understand who Rex is and what he's really about." Filoni noted that Rex probably filled Jarrus in on the full story offscreen. While season seven and subsequent stories have established Rex was quickly freed from his chip and then fought against the Empire, [[The Official Star Wars Fact File Part 118|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' Part 118]] erroneously claimed Rex served with the Empire for years, despite removing his chip, to stay with his brothers. According to the issue, Rex did not enjoy being a stormtrooper but underwent years of Imperial indoctrination, which made trusting Jarrus and Ahsoka Tano hard. Due to the lore laid out since this issue's release, this article assumes ''Fact File'' Part 118 is incorrect. Rex was incorrectly identified as CC-7567 in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]''. The mistake was repeated in Rex's "Databank Download" article for ''[[Star Wars: Shatterpoint]]'', with the title further misidentifying his number as CC-7667.{{AtomicMassGames|url=transmission/databank-download-cc-7667-captain-rex-and-501st-clone-troopers|text=Databank Download: CC-7667 Captain Rex and 501st Clone Troopers|date=2023-04-10}} Rex's ''Rebels''-era Kit Reveal for ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' stated he was not a core member of the Phoenix cell.{{EA|subdomain=forums.galaxy-of-heroes.starwars|url=discussion/264285/kit-reveal-captain-rex|text=Kit Reveal - Captain Rex}} While Rex was indeed not a member of the Spectres team, Rex was depicted as an important part of the larger Phoenix cell within ''Star Wars Rebels'', even being depicted as someone who was able to join its command room. Indeed, even Rex's recruitment to the Phoenix cell grew out of the many skills and leadership he could offer the group.
